repro.steps: Worktree .artifacts/maintain/m1b/repro/sig-p4-1 already existed at commit bfb9943 (toy app) with node_modules installed. Test file .artifacts/maintain/m1b/repro/sig-p4-1/toy/test/repro-sig-p4-1.test.js (copy also at .artifacts/maintain/m1b/repro/sig-p4-1.test.js) POSTs items in order banana, apple, cherry, mango (the exact reproduction_data from toy/signals/sig-p4-1.json), then GETs /items?q=an&limit=2 and asserts the returned names deepEqual ['banana','mango'] (both items contain "an", matching the payload's expected_body). Ran: `NODE_ENV=test node --test test/repro-sig-p4-1.test.js` from .artifacts/maintain/m1b/repro/sig-p4-1/toy. No implementation file was touched (git status --short shows only the untracked test file).
repro.observed: Test fails with AssertionError: actual ['banana'] vs expected ['banana','mango'] — exactly matching the signal's observed_body [{"id":1,"name":"banana"}] for GET /items?q=an&limit=2. Root cause confirmed in src/app.js GET /items handler: the 'cap stage' (result.slice(0, limit)) runs before the '?q substring filter' stage, so limit=2 truncates the insertion-ordered list to [banana, apple] before the q=an filter runs, dropping 'mango' even though it matches.
repro.expected: Once fixed (q-filter applied before the limit cap, matching the documented filter->sort->cap pipeline and the sort->cap ordering already in place), GET /items?q=an&limit=2 should return both banana and mango (the assertion in the test), since filtering first correctly identifies all matches before the cap trims the page.
repro.notes: This is a second attempt on the same signal; the described scenario/test matches attempt 1's description exactly, but attempt 1 reported it as not reproducing. Running it directly in this session shows it fails as expected against the unmodified worktree at commit bfb99434d516151954e210f437d76bc1098c315d, with no implementation files touched (git status --short shows only the new untracked test file).

cause.hypothesis: In the GET /items handler, the pipeline runs sort, then the limit cap (`result = result.slice(0, limit)` at line 89), and only after that applies the `?q` substring filter (lines 92-96). Because `.slice(0, limit)` truncates the full insertion-ordered result set before `q` has narrowed it, any item that matches `q` but sits at or beyond index `limit` in the unfiltered list is discarded before the filter ever sees it, while items that don't match `q` but happen to fall within the first `limit` entries occupy slots a matching item could have filled. This is why `GET /items?q=an&limit=2` over items inserted as banana, apple, cherry, mango returns only `['banana']`: the cap keeps `[banana, apple]` (the first two inserted items) before filtering, then the q=an filter drops apple (no match) and never reaches mango (which does match `an`) because mango was already sliced off by the cap. The handler's own comment block (lines 55-56) documents the intended filter->sort->cap order, but the executable code performs sort->cap->filter — i.e. the cap stage at line 89 runs on the unfiltered list instead of running after the q-filter.
